HOLOCAUST SURVIVOR

By: Latashia Naidoo | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
She survived 3 concentration camps, and is one of the oldest living Holocaust survivors in the world. Now Cape Town's Ella Blumental is sharing er story with the world.

Unique Selling Point:
Ella Blumenthal is South Africa's oldest living Holocaust survivor. Now her tragic life story is being immortalised on film.

Summary:
At the age of 101, Ella Blumenthal has lived an extraordinary life - tinged with pockets of happiness, but also, unspeakable tragedies.
The Camps Bay resident - who was born in Warsaw, Poland - is South Africa’s oldest living Holocaust survivor.
She survived three concentration camps in Nazi-occupied Poland in the 1940’s - including the notorious Auschwitz.

Ella is now the subject of a new documentary, I Am Here, which catalogues her remarkable life story, and her incredible will to live.
Filmmaker Jordy Sank grew up hearing about Ella and her story of survival within his community, and spent two years making the film - which was released internationally in 2022, and has already won numerous awards.
Ella is unbelievably spritely, vivacious, and positive - and says her long life and secret to happiness is rooted in a foundation of ‘forgiveness’.



Further information:
Ella's story encapsulates the power of the human spirit to success despite adversity. It's a story of overcoming the brutalities of war and surviving the gas chamber and losing 18 members of her family; to becoming a diamond trader for the Polish Jews smuggling Nazi diamonds, to modeling in Paris, and then marrying a South African man and starting a family here.

This a story of triumphs over tragedies, and of how forgiveness can heal even the most traumatic of wounds.

Script:


HOLOCAUST SURVIVOR - FINAL:

ELLA:
“When I came I saw so many bodies, and I said to myself: “I survived the Warsaw Ghetto, I survived Merdanik, I survived the gas chamber, I survived Auschwitz. No, I must not stay here and end my life like this bodies! No, I must live!

VO:
Ella Blumenthal has lived through one of history’ darkest chapters…

VO:
At the age of a hundred and one, she is South Africa’s oldest living holocaust survivor…

VO:
Now her extraordinary story of defying death time and time again…
has been documented…

VO:
In an award-winning documentary by a team of South African filmmakers…

That recounts her harrowing journey from the Warsaw Ghetto, to three concentration camps in Nazi-occupied Poland during the Second World War - to present day Cape Town…

VO:
Meeting Ella… it’s easy to see why she’s so remarkable…

Even in her twilight years… her zest for life is infectious…

The only thing that gives away her age is a slight hearing problem…

But her eye for style is still spot on - decades after a long career in fashion…

(ELLA PUTTING ON CLAIRE’S JACKET, POSING FOR PIC:)
Claire: Okay, you can wear it…
Ella: Give it to me. Very nice, very nice, thank you - I want to look at the label…
Claire: It’s only Woolworths, it’s not Dior, it’s not Chanel…
Ella: Oppi!

VO:
Ella was born in Warsaw, Poland, in 1921, the youngest of seven children…

CLAIRE: What was it like growing up in Poland?

ELLA: I was a happy youngster, and running around. Instead of school, I used to sometimes go and get ice-creams. And I was naughty! I was a naughty girl. My teacher was wearing a wig, so I got somebody to put off the lights, and I pulled off the wig!”

CLAIRE: Gasps… “You were a naughty girl!”

VO:
Then the war broke out…

VO:
And one by one - 23 members of her family were murdered by the Nazis…

VO:
Only Ella and her niece Roma eventually survived…

VO:
From 1943 to 1945, they were sent to three Nazi death camps: Majdanek, Auschwitz, and Bergen-Belsen…

ELLA: At night, middle of the night, they chased us out, and it was so quiet, you could see the stars but you could hear nothing. Even the trees were not moving, the leaves. And we were ordered to get into a bathhouse. But it wasn’t a bathhouse - it was a gas chamber.
When we were inside we realised that the gas was going to come down any minute, it’s just a little bit time for us to stay alive.

CLAIRE: But then they didn't gas you… what happened?

ELLA: I was holding my niece’s hand, and I was whispering: “Don’t be afraid, it won’t even hurt, and it won’t take long. We will soon get together with our loved ones.” At this very moment, the heavy doors open, and an SS man walked in. “Quiet! You are not going to be gassed!” We couldn’t believe it!

LINK: Looking at these pictures of Ella’s life, it’s impossible to imagine the trauma, torture, and immense loss she endured… behind these smiling eyes.

VO:
I Am Here is a portrait of Ella’s survival…

And tells the story she kept close to her heart for more than seven decades…

EVELYN:
From the time that I knew that she had had this trauma in her life, I had this intense desire - which I still do - to protect her. And to prevent her having to undergo any further trauma.

VO:
Dr Evelyn Kaplan is the youngest of Ella’s four children…

EVELYN: I realised as I was growing up there was something different, there was something amiss in the family. Also, because she used to have terrible nightmares. And I remember as a small child, I remember her screaming at night and me saying to her: “Are you all right?”, and she would scream, “They’re taking my children!” And I said, “but I’m here!” So those sort of things. And she had this scar on her arm; I asked her where the scar was from, and she said she had an accident.
Even in my mind had imprinted in my mind this impression of an accident, the glass going through her arm… I was aware of an undercurrent of something being different.

VO: The scar hid a tragic secret: her concentration camp number…

CLAIRE LINK:
How do you forgive the unforgivable? How do you move past unimaginable trauma? These are questions Ella has asked herself for decades. But she has found it in her heart to forgive, and has made it her mission to bring peace and healing to the world.

VO:
In April 1945, Ella, Roma, and hundreds of thousands of other Jews…
were finally liberated…

ELLA: The British tanks came in with the soldiers on it, and they shouted: “You are liberated! You are free!

VO:
The pair moved to Paris soon after… where Ella worked in a somewhat un-kosher profession - as a smuggler of diamonds and foreign currency for some wealthy Jewish businessmen.

ELLA: I went to Paris, to France… I managed to find a very fine job, a little bit, not so legal, but now I can tell you. If I had been caught, I would’ve been in prison.

VO:
Two years later, she joined Roma in Tel Aviv - where she met her future husband, Isaac.

They were married after just 13 days… and relocated to Johannesburg’s East Rand shortly after.

There, she had four children, and opened a successful clothing store in Brakpan… specialising in women’s fashion…

No wonder she’s given me fashion tips!

VO:
But despite rebuilding a beautiful new life for herself…

Ella chose to bury her past…

ELLA - I had a number here, can you see? Soon after I arrived, my husband’s family told me: “You should try and forget, your past, your terrible time in the Ghetto’s, so you should have it removed.”
*** I didn’t want to remember. I came out of such a terrible place… Hell! I came out of hell!

VO:
In 2004, she returned to Poland for the first time…
And re-visited the place she was condemned to death… Auschwitz…

VO:
Almost two decades later… her story is finally being shared with the world…

VO:
I Am Here was released internationally last year…
The filmmakers say audiences have resonated with Ella’s larger-than-life personality, and her resilience…

Gabriella: “It’s not a film that’s only for audiences that have a connection to the Holocaust. This is a film for each one of us, and especially in a South African context, who have a history of trauma, a history of discrimination. And can resonate with how Ella has overcome this in her own way.

VO:
In the face of unfathomable hate, Ella has gone on to live a life of happiness, tolerance, and forgiveness…

ELLA:
The hate - that is what kills us. Why does religion, or colour, does it matter? We’ve all got the same blood under our skins. Life is so beautiful. Look at the mountains, look at the sea, look at the air we’re breathing. So why hate each other?


**********

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): She survived 3 concentration camps, and is one of the oldest living Holocaust survivors in the world. Now Cape Town's Ella Blumental is sharing er story with the world.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Ella Blumenthal is South Africa's oldest living Holocaust survivor. Now her tragic life story is being immortalised on film.
metadata.Summary: At the age of 101, Ella Blumenthal has lived an extraordinary life - tinged with pockets of happiness, but also, unspeakable tragedies. The Camps Bay resident - who was born in Warsaw, Poland - is South Africa’s oldest living Holocaust survivor. She survived three concentration camps in Nazi-occupied Poland in the 1940’s - including the notorious Auschwitz. Ella is now the subject of a new documentary, I Am Here, which catalogues her remarkable life story, and her incredible will to live. Filmmaker Jordy Sank grew up hearing about Ella and her story of survival within his community, and spent two years making the film - which was released internationally in 2022, and has already won numerous awards. Ella is unbelievably spritely, vivacious, and positive - and says her long life and secret to happiness is rooted in a foundation of ‘forgiveness’.
metadata.Further information: Ella's story encapsulates the power of the human spirit to success despite adversity. It's a story of overcoming the brutalities of war and surviving the gas chamber and losing 18 members of her family; to becoming a diamond trader for the Polish Jews smuggling Nazi diamonds, to modeling in Paris, and then marrying a South African man and starting a family here. This a story of triumphs over tragedies, and of how forgiveness can heal even the most traumatic of wounds.
